why_trail.why: The gate has three halves and one hard ordering constraint I did not have before reading: the sweep alone leaves the suite red because test_mcp_adoption.py MANDATES the text (nine assertions), so the corpus edit and the test inversion must land together. The guard is the spec and is fenced. Counting unit is occurrences, not lines or files: COMMANDER_SPINE.archive carries two <engine> tokens on one line, and the overlay's 16 occurrences sit in 6 JSON leaves plus .baseline/ mirrors. The three second-checklist sites are reworded, not deleted, and the reword may name the engine but must not show a command line or a stand-in followed by an engine verb.

The 13 clauses were never one kind of thing, and the sweep had to reflect that. 10 were dead weight beside a working door and came out with the sentence that framed them as a choice ("by default ... otherwise"), which was itself the second-path idea in grammar. 3 name a case the door provably cannot reach — a checklist that is not the spine this process is bound to — so they were reworded to state the mechanism (one door drives one spine at a time; it refuses to rebind while its owner holds the lease) and to name the bundled engine as the only path, without writing a command line. The word "fallback" is now stated as wrong for that case, because there is no working primary. Two waiver/attach sites also carried an engine command line and were converted to the equivalent door-tool call rather than deleted, since a human still needs to know how to waive.

The overlay is not a copy to keep in sync as a courtesy — it is the copy an agent in this repo actually instantiates from, so before this step the launch order's acceptance test still failed on a swept skills/ tree. Measured before the propagation: 16 <engine> and 18 clause occurrences across 10 files (5 visible + 5 .baseline/ mirrors), and all ten were blob-identical to their UNSWEPT skills/ sources at HEAD — which is what made whole-file propagation safe rather than a merge. Proved after: skills source, overlay copy and baseline mirror share one blob OID for all five files, and a fresh spine instantiated from the overlay COMMANDER template hands a Commander init and plan imperatives carrying zero of either pattern.

Two things the handoff could not have known, found while inverting. First, the two CLI assertions on commander-core.md shared a paragraph LOCATOR keyed to the text being deleted ('<engine> attach'), so after the sweep the door-affirmative half -- explicitly not mine to weaken -- would have died with an unrelated "has the CLI line moved?" message; the locator had to move to the door side to keep that half alive. Second, Tier2's whole-file absence check cannot be `checklist_engine.py not in text`, the standard the two-file precedent uses: skills/explorer/SKILL.md carries a scripts manifest naming the engine as a component, which is exactly the prose-vs-command line the epic drew and the guard pins in both directions. Tier2 is therefore scoped to the clause and the placeholder, Tier4 stays whole-file because a template has no manifest, and both reasons are written in the code. I also deleted a tenth mandate the handoff's table missed -- test_states_identity_trade_rule -- which required lane D2's file to carry a sentence routing a dispatched subagent to the CLI for its own plan, a claim run_crew.py --spine already made false.

There is no generator for this census -- I looked: verify_retirement.py has only a scan CLI, and its own comment ("one code path, used by the leg AND by whatever seeds the census") describes a seeding path nothing in the repo actually implements. So the handoff's "do not hand-edit it if a generator exists" resolves to: derive the new entries MECHANICALLY through that same code path rather than retyping them. I did -- store_mention_sites() produced the new normalized lines, load_approved() and _read_lines() identified the two stale ones, and the swap was refused unless each was a clean 1:1 pairing within its own file. Both reasons and the census's structure are untouched; only the two quoted imperative lines moved, which is exactly what my sweep changed.

The proof is discriminating in the way the cold critic demanded, and the evidence for that is positional: the reintroduced clause is flagged at skills/interrogator/SKILL.md:28, one line below the reworded text at :27 that says nearly the same thing about the same mechanism and is flagged by nothing, in either direction of the run. So the guard is separating the two sentences, not the two files. I also found that close criterion 5's own filter command cannot print nothing while the guard is red at all: the guard's census sentence names '.agent-work/templates/', and the criterion's regex matches it out of that prose. The site list itself is empty -- shown with a filter anchored to whole address lines -- so this is a defect in the criterion's command, not in the sweep.

The guard now names exactly four addresses, all of them inside skills/workbench/ -- SKILL.md:37 and checklist-engine.md:5,41,45 -- which is lane D2's file set and the measured, expected residual this lane cannot clear. Nothing under skills/ outside workbench, nothing under specs/, and nothing under .agent-work/templates/ survives, which is the part that proves the overlay sweep landed rather than the skills/ sweep alone. All five doctrine templates share one blob OID across source, overlay copy and .baseline/ mirror.

The result carries what a reviewer cannot reconstruct from the diff: which of the ten mandates were inverted versus deleted and the reason for each, the two locator/scoping findings that changed how the inversion had to be written, the measured absence of a census generator, and the defect in close criterion 5's own filter command. It also states the one real coverage loss plainly -- skills/workbench/SKILL.md's paragraph-scoped door assertion, dropped because the file is fenced this wave -- rather than letting the deletion read as a wash.

amendments.reason: My own m3 check was a bare name grep over the whole file, so it cannot tell a DELETED assertion from a deliberate historical citation of one. The inversion the handoff asked for requires exactly those citations: the new docstrings name test_field_still_carries_cli_fallback, test_still_names_cli_invocation and test_door_section_itself_keeps_the_cli to record what was inverted, what was deleted, and why -- which is how a future reader sees continuity rather than a reversal. Rescoped to the `def ` line, which is what "the assertion no longer exists" actually means, and widened to all eight retired names so it is stricter than before. Reintroducing any of them still fails it.

Close criterion 5's filter, which I copied verbatim into this check, has a false positive it cannot avoid: every guard failure message carries the census sentence "(101 under skills/, 2 under specs/, 113 under .agent-work/templates/)", and the criterion's own regex matches ".agent-work/templates/" out of that prose. So the command can only print nothing when the guard is entirely green, which this lane cannot reach before lane D2 merges -- the very situation the criterion was written to accommodate. Rescoped to extract whole ADDRESS lines, which is the shape _sites() actually emits ("    <path>[:<line>]" on its own line), after stripping pytest's "E " prefix. Strictly more falsifiable than the original: it still names every real site, and it no longer passes or fails on prose. Reported as a handoff defect rather than smoothed over.
